deed: הצבא הישראלי הקים בית חולים שדה בהאיטי — 89 שעות אחרי רעידת האדמה
title: The IDF set up a field hospital in Haiti 89 hours after the earthquake and registered 1,111 patients there

trailer.text: The Israel Defense Forces Medical Corps dispatched a field hospital unit to Haiti following an earthquake.
On January 12, 2010, a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Haiti, and it caused severe damage to buildings throughout the capital, Port-au-Prince.
The force's mission was to establish a field hospital and to give medical support to as many people as possible.
According to the authors of the abstract, the hospital started operating in Port-au-Prince 89 hours after the earthquake.
During 10 days of operation, the system registered 1,111 patients, and according to the article, 16 babies were born there.

stations.title: A city without electricity, water or food

paragraphs.text: On January 12, 2010, a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Haiti.
The earthquake caused severe damage to buildings throughout the capital, Port-au-Prince.
The International Red Cross estimated that about three million people were affected.
In a report, Radian described a city without electricity, without water and without food.
The telephone lines had collapsed, and people were buried under the rubble.
According to World Bank data, Haiti's national income per head in 2010 was about $1,140, and it is one of the poorest countries in the world.
According to the article, about half of Haiti's population was unregistered and had no identification documents, even before the earthquake.
The force's primary mission was to establish a field hospital in Haiti and to give medical support to as many people as possible.
According to the abstract, the government of Israel dispatched a military task force that included medical personnel from the IDF Medical Corps.

Three of the physicians and one of the nurses who served at the hospital were staffers of Jerusalem’s Shaare Zedek Medical Center, and another staff member worked with a different non-profit organization in the disaster area; according to the article, together they were the largest delegation from a single Israeli hospital.
According to the Jewish Journal reporter, 30 tons of aid were flown from Israel to the victims in Haiti.
According to J., because planes could not land safely in Port-au-Prince, most of the medical and other supplies were sent to Santo Domingo, then trucked daily into the Haitian capital.
Daniel Biran, Israel's ambassador of administrative affairs, who oversees 28 embassies in North America, arrived in Haiti on January 14 via Santo Domingo, according to J.
According to Biran, the Israeli army eats kosher food even in emergency situations.
The hospital was set up in tents.
According to J., eighteen Israeli civilians and 218 reserve soldiers built and maintained two surgical tents, a pediatrics tent, a radiology tent and a tent for newborn or premature babies.
The hospital had seven departments, including medicine, surgery and orthopedics.
According to Merin, the hospital had a blood bank, an X-ray facility, and a large amount of equipment and medications.
According to the authors of the abstract, the hospital started operating 89 hours after the earthquake.
According to Biran, it was immediately flooded with hundreds of patients.
According to J., Israel was the first country to set up a field hospital after the earthquake in Haiti.
According to Gali Weiss, 25 Jews reside in the Haitian capital.
Dr. Ofer Merin served as chief surgeon and was in charge of intensive care.
The doctors appointed an ethics committee, which decided which victims would be admitted and which had a reasonable chance of survival.
According to Gali Weiss, the nurses' shifts were officially 12 hours on and 12 hours off, but usually lasted longer.
According to Dr. Ehud Lebel, fractures were treated without open surgery, with metal pins inserted from the outside to set the bones.
There were no surgical drills, so the orthopedic surgeons drilled into bones with ordinary do-it-yourself electric drills.
The hospital lacked even operating tables. Additional tables arrived when a US Navy ship came into port and donated them to the Israeli facility.
According to Dr. Carmi Bartal, by that evening 210 casualties had been admitted, 70 operations had been performed and there had been four births.
According to him, a 19-year-old young woman arrived who had lain for six days with a concrete wall on her arm.
Bartal said that in the first days there was no coordination between the aid organizations.

stations.title: A photo, a CD and a computer

paragraphs.text: The hospital's medical informatics team, three people, set up and maintained the computer system.
According to the article, the system was fully operational within six hours of the team's arrival at the site, 89 hours after the earthquake.
The network and system up times were more than 99.9%.
According to the article, a backup paper record was also kept for each patient.
According to Merin, nobody in Haiti has identity cards, so the photos were used to keep track of patients and for relatives to identify them.
According to the article, several family members were able to locate their relatives in the photo database and receive information about their condition.
According to the article on the conference at Shaare Zedek, each patient was discharged – usually to the street – with a CD containing his personal medical file, including x-rays and scans.

According to the authors of the paper, and to the best of their knowledge, the deployment in Haiti was the first operational installation of a medical information system and an electronic medical record in a field hospital.
During 10 days of operation, the system registered 1,111 patients.
According to the article, 737 of them were admitted as inpatients.
According to the abstract, 363 of the patients were children under the age of 18.
By the ninth day, most patients were already coming because of a non-traumatic cause, according to the abstract.
16 babies were born.
According to the abstract, the hospital's neonatal unit was the only one in the affected area.
An account of Prof. Eli Schwartz’s work with the NATAN organization, outside the field hospital, says that the Israelis established a school for children, mostly orphans, who learned amid the rubble.
According to J., the team erected one more tent for patients who had finished treatment and had no home to return to.
According to J., the IDF search-and-rescue force led or participated in the rescue of four people.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the Israeli hospital was by far the best-organized and best-equipped medical facility in Port-au-Prince, and received great praise from around the world.
According to J., the international media gave wide coverage to Biran and the Israeli professionals for the efficiency with which they set up a functioning hospital.
Prof. Eli Schwartz said that no country in the world could send medical aid so quickly.
Lebel said he was very proud of what the IDF team had done.
According to the Jerusalem Post, in such a field hospital patients are not asked for informed consent, and privacy is a luxury.
According to Merin, the team could not speak with the patients in their own language, which made it easier to give care without consent and consultation, but took an emotional toll.
Lebel admitted that they had to compromise on equipment, even on gloves.

The ethics committees discussed whether to amputate all necrotic limbs: when life was in immediate danger they were amputated, but when both legs were rotting, the surgeons faced the dilemma of sending a completely helpless victim into the street where follow-up was not available.
According to Goldberg, a baby was born weighing 900 grams, and it was decided not to resuscitate, because there was no way to keep it alive.
Lebel said that mistakes were also made, but the team helped all kinds of people.

disagreements.question: How many people died in the disaster?

versions.says: Abstract by members of the Israeli team: an estimated 230,000 dead, about 250,000 injured and more than one million who lost their homes
World Health Organization, as reported at the start of the operation: between 50 thousand and 100 thousand dead
Estimates from the first days: about 50 thousand dead
Abstract in the journal Prehospital and Disaster Medicine: 230 people, including 121 medical personnel
Summary of the NEJM article: the Israeli government dispatched 230 military task force personnel.
Jerusalem Post: the hospital staff numbered 121, including 40 doctors, 20 nurses, 20 paramedics and medics, and 20 technicians and administrators
Report from the start of the operation: a jumbo jet with 220 people, including 120 doctors and medical staff

disagreements.question: When did the team leave Israel?

versions.says: Authors of the abstract: about 50 hours after the earthquake
Jerusalem Post: less than 24 hours after the earthquake

disagreements.question: Where was the hospital set up?

versions.says: The article: on a soccer field near Port-au-Prince airport
Jerusalem Post: on a soccer field in the center of the capital
J.: in the backyard of one of Haiti's few Jewish residents

disagreements.question: How long did it take to set up the hospital?

versions.says: Authors of the abstract: the hospital started operating 89 hours after the earthquake
Daniel Biran: the hospital was ready within eight hours
Jewish Journal reporter: within 6 hours of the team's arrival from Israel

disagreements.question: How many computers did the hospital have?

versions.says: Ofer Merin: 10 laptop computers
The article: 14 workstations, laptop computers

disagreements.question: How many operations were performed at the hospital?

versions.says: The article: 242 operations
The abstract: 244 operations
Ofer Merin: 315 operations
The Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as quoted in J.: 319 successful surgeries

disagreements.question: How many cesarean deliveries were there?

versions.says: The Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as quoted in J.: three
Dr. Doron Goldberg: six, even though a cesarean section was not the preferred means of delivery under camp conditions

disagreements.question: How many deaths were there at the hospital?

versions.says: The abstract: 17
Ofer Merin: only 13, during a two-week stay

disagreements.question: Which patients got a CD at discharge, and what was on it?

versions.says: The Jerusalem Post, on the Shaare Zedek conference: every patient was discharged, usually to the street, with a CD holding his personal medical file, including x-rays and scans
Paper by the team (Levy, Merin et al.): only patients discharged to another medical facility got a printed discharge summary and a CD with their imaging studies

disagreements.question: How many people set up the hospital, and how many operating rooms did it have?

versions.says: J.: eighteen civilians and 218 reserve soldiers built and maintained two surgical tents
The hospital commanders in NEJM: a task force of 230 people, and the hospital had one operating room with a single table

disagreements.question: Who set up the first field hospital after the earthquake?

versions.says: J.: Israel was the first country to set up a field hospital
The US CDC: the University of Miami Global Institute/Project Medishare set up the first field hospital in Port-au-Prince, on January 13, 2010

claims.text: חיל הרפואה של צה"ל (Israel Defense Force) שלח יחידת בית חולים שדה בעקבות רעידת האדמה.
claims.quote: the Israel Defense Force Medical Corps dispatched a field hospital unit

claims.text: ב-12 בינואר 2010 פקדה את האיטי רעידת אדמה בעוצמה של 7.0.
claims.quote: On January 12, 2010, a magnitude 7.0 Mw earthquake struck Haiti.

claims.text: רעידת האדמה גרמה נזק חמור לבניינים ברחבי הבירה פורט-או-פראנס.
claims.quote: The earthquake caused severe damage to buildings throughout the capital city Port au Prince.

claims.text: המשימה העיקרית של הכוח הייתה להקים בית חולים שדה בהאיטי ולתת סיוע רפואי למספר רב ככל האפשר של אנשים.
claims.quote: The force's primary mission was to establish a field hospital in Haiti and to give medical support to as many people as possible.

claims.text: לפי כותבי התקציר, הצוות יצא מישראל כ-50 שעות אחרי הרעידה ובית החולים החל לפעול בפורט-או-פראנס 89 שעות אחריה.
claims.quote: We left Israel about 50 hours after the Earthquake and the field hospital started operating at Porte-Au-Prince 89 hours after the earthquake.

claims.text: במהלך 10 ימי פעילות רשמה המערכת 1,111 מטופלים.
claims.quote: During 10 days of operation, the system registered 1111 patients.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, 737 מהמטופלים אושפזו, בוצעו 242 ניתוחים ונולדו 16 תינוקות.
claims.quote: 737 of them were admitted as inpatients, 242 operations were performed in the operating room, and 16 babies were born.

claims.text: לפי J., השהות הישראלית נמשכה מ-15 עד 27 בינואר.
claims.quote: During the Israelis’ stay from Jan. 15 to 27, the team treated more than 1,110 patients

claims.text: לפי התקציר, היו 16 לידות, 244 ניתוחים ו-17 מקרי מוות בבית החולים.
claims.quote: There were 16 deliveries, 5 Neonates, 244 Operations and 17 Intra-hospital deaths.

claims.text: הצלב האדום הבינלאומי העריך שכשלושה מיליון בני אדם נפגעו מהרעידה.
claims.quote: The International Red Cross estimated that about three million people were affected by the quake.

claims.text: עד שנאמר בדיווח, תיאר רדיאן עיר ללא חשמל, מים ואוכל, עם קווי טלפון שקרסו ואנשים קבורים מתחת להריסות.
claims.quote: אין חשמל ואין מים ואין אוכל. קווי הטלפון קרסו. אנשים קבורים מתחת להריסות ואין צוותי חילוץ שמנסים להוציא אותם משם.

claims.text: לפי האחות הראשית גלי וייס, ההכנסה השנתית לנפש בהאיטי היא 380 דולר, והיא אחת המדינות העניות בעולם.
claims.quote: The annual per capita income is $380, making it one of the poorest places in the world.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, כמחצית מאוכלוסיית האיטי אינה רשומה ואין לה מסמכי זהות, עוד לפני רעידת האדמה.
claims.quote: approximately half the population in the country is unregistered and has no identification documents

claims.text: לפי התקציר, ממשלת ישראל שלחה כוח משימה צבאי של 230 איש, ובהם 121 אנשי צוות רפואי מחיל הרפואה של צה"ל.
claims.quote: The government of Israel dispatched a military task force consisting of 230 people. 121 of them were medical personnel from the IDF Medical Corps.

claims.text: שלושה רופאים ואחות אחת מהמרכז הרפואי שערי צדק בירושלים שירתו בבית החולים, המשלחת הגדולה ביותר מבית חולים ישראלי בודד.

claims.text: לבל אמר שהוא גאה מאוד במה שעשה צוות צה"ל.
claims.quote: Lebel was very proud of what the IDF team had done

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בבית חולים שדה כזה לא מבקשים הסכמה מדעת מהמטופלים והפרטיות היא מותרות.
claims.quote: None of the sick or wounded is asked for his informed consent; providing privacy is an undreamed-of luxury

claims.text: לפי מרין, אי היכולת לתקשר עם המטופלים בשפתם הקלה בכך שרק סיפקו טיפול בלי הסכמה והתייעצות, אך גבתה מחיר רגשי.
claims.quote: being unable to communicate with patients in their native tongue made it easier because they had only to give medical care without consent and consultation

claims.text: לבל הודה שנאלצו להתפשר על ציוד, אפילו על כפפות.
claims.quote: We had to compromise on equipment, even gloves

claims.text: הכירורגים התלבטו אם לשלוח קורבן חסר ישע לרחוב, שבו אין המשך טיפול, כשרגליו נרקבות.
claims.quote: the surgeons faced the dilemma of sending a completely helpless victim into the street where follow-up was not available.

claims.text: לדברי גולדברג, נולד תינוק במשקל 900 גרם, והוחלט לא לשקם אותו כי אי אפשר היה להשאירו בחיים.
claims.quote: One baby was born at 900 grams, but we decided not to resuscitate, as there was no way it could have been kept alive.

claims.text: לבל אמר שנעשו גם טעויות, אך הצוות עזר לכל מיני אנשים.
claims.quote: We also made some mistakes, but we helped all kinds of people.

claims.text: לפי תקציר של אנשי הצוות הישראלי, באזור נהרגו לפי הערכה 230,000 בני אדם, כ-250,000 נפצעו ולמעלה ממיליון איבדו את בתיהם.
claims.quote: The region suffered an estimated 230,000 fatalities with approximately 250,000 injured and more than one million people who lost their houses.

claims.text: לפי הערכת ארגון הבריאות העולמי, כפי שדווח בתחילת הפעילות, נהרגו בין 50 אלף ל-100 אלף בני אדם.
claims.quote: על פי הערכת ארגון הבריאות העולמי, בין 50 אלף ל-100 אלף נהרגו

claims.text: לפי הערכות שפורסמו בימים הראשונים, כ-50 אלף בני אדם נהרגו באסון.
claims.quote: ועל פי ההערכות, כ-50 אלף בני אדם נהרגו באסון

claims.text: לפי תקציר ה-NEJM, ממשלת ישראל שלחה 230 אנשי כוח משימה צבאי לתמיכה בבית החולים.
claims.quote: The Israeli government dispatched 230 military task force personnel to support this field hospital.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, צוות בית החולים מנה 121 איש: 40 רופאים, 20 אחיות, 20 חובשים ופראמדיקים, ו-20 טכנאי מעבדה ורנטגן ואנשי מנהלה.
claims.quote: was staffed by a 121-member team with 40 doctors, 20 nurses, 20 paramedics and medics, 20 lab and X-ray technicians and administrators.

claims.text: לפי דיווח מתחילת הפעילות, מטוס ג'מבו עם 220 איש, ובהם 120 רופאים ואנשי צוות רפואי, נחת בפורט-או-פראנס.
claims.quote: מטוס ג'מבו ועליו 220 איש, בהם 120 רופאים ואנשי צוות רפואי נחת בבירה פורט או-פראנס.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, צוות צה"ל טס להאיטי פחות מ-24 שעות אחרי הרעידה.
claims.quote: the Israel Defense Forces team that flew to Haiti less than 24 hours after the horrific earthquake that shook Port-au-Prince

claims.text: לפי המאמר, בית החולים הוקם במגרש כדורגל ליד שדה התעופה של פורט-או-פראנס.
claims.quote: which set up a field hospital at the soccer field near Port au Prince airport

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, המתקן הישראלי הוקם כאוהלים מסודרים במגרש כדורגל במרכז הבירה.
claims.quote: The Israeli facility, set up as neatly arranged tents in a soccer field in the capital’s center

claims.text: לפי J., מיקום בית החולים נקבע בסופו של דבר בחצר האחורית של אחד מהתושבים היהודים המעטים בהאיטי.
claims.quote: which ended up being the backyard of one of Haiti’s few Jewish residents

claims.text: לפי כתב ה-Jewish Journal, בית החולים של צה"ל הוקם בתוך 6 שעות מהגעת הצוות מישראל.
claims.quote: The IDF Field hospital set up in Haiti was set-up in a matter of 6 hours after the arrival of the team from Israel.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, 14 עמדות עבודה, מחשבים ניידים, פוזרו בבית החולים.
claims.quote: Fourteen workstations were distributed throughout the hospital. We elected to use laptop computers as the workstation hardware

claims.text: לדברי עופר מרין, טופלו 1,111 פצועים וחולים ובוצעו 315 ניתוחים.
claims.quote: A total of 1,111 wounded and sick were treated, and 315 operations were performed.

claims.text: לפי משרד החוץ הישראלי, כפי שצוטט ב-J., הצוות ביצע 319 ניתוחים מוצלחים וילדו 16 תינוקות, מהם שלושה בניתוח קיסרי.
claims.quote: the team treated more than 1,110 patients, did 319 successful surgeries and delivered 16 babies, including three by caesarean section, according to the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

claims.text: לדברי ד"ר דורון גולדברג, בוצעו שישה ניתוחים קיסריים, אף שלא היו הדרך המועדפת בתנאי המחנה.
claims.quote: There were six cesarean sections, even though that was not the preferred means of delivery under camp conditions.

claims.text: לדברי מרין, 13 אנשים בלבד שטופלו בבית החולים מתו במהלך שהות של שבועיים.
claims.quote: Only 13 people treated in the tent hospital died during the two-week stay.

claims.text: ג'רוזלם פוסט, על הכנס בשערי צדק: כל מטופל שוחרר, בדרך כלל לרחוב, עם דיסק ובו התיק הרפואי האישי שלו, כולל צילומי רנטגן וסריקות
claims.quote: each patient was discharged – usually to the street – with a CD containing his personal medical file

quote_translations.c9: There is no electricity and there is no water and there is no food. The telephone lines have collapsed. People are buried under the rubble and there are no rescue teams trying to get them out of there.
quote_translations.c46: So far we have admitted 210 casualties, performed 70 operations and four deliveries
quote_translations.c47: A 19-year-old young woman came to us who had lain for six days with a concrete wall on her arm
quote_translations.c48: We are trying to coordinate everything with the organizations around us, but there is no coordination.
quote_translations.c5: According to the World Health Organization's estimate, between 50 thousand and 100 thousand were killed
quote_translations.c6: And according to the estimates, about 50 thousand people were killed in the disaster
